title: The teaching as teacher
hook: after I am gone, the dhamma and discipline will be your teacher

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ananda in the doorway, and your line, you've done well, Ananda. Who did you thank by name? Today, the question every grieving student asks: who teaches us now? Day five hundred fifty-one.

A piano teacher dies. Her students still have the exercises she wrote in pencil on their sheet music, the habits she drilled into their hands, the sound of her voice saying slower. Do they have a teacher anymore? In one sense, no. In another, she's in every scale they play. The Buddha is lying between the sal trees, and he can see this question forming in Ananda's mind before Ananda says it. So he answers it first. Today: the teaching as teacher.
screen: `PENCIL MARKS ON THE SHEET MUSIC.` → `DO THEY STILL HAVE A TEACHER?` → `HE ANSWERS BEFORE IT'S ASKED.`

segments.voice: It may be, Ananda, he says, that some of you will think: the teacher's word is over; we have no teacher. Don't see it that way. The Dhamma and the discipline that I have taught and laid down for you, that will be your teacher when I am gone. In Pali the pair is dhamma-vinaya: the teaching, and the training rules that shape a community's life. Notice what he doesn't do. He doesn't name a successor. He doesn't appoint a council. Earlier on this road he said he'd never thought of himself as the community's leader, and he stays consistent to the end. The teacher becomes something anyone can open. Then come a few practical instructions, and then a remarkable invitation. He asks the gathered monks: if any of you has a doubt or a question about the Buddha, the teaching, the community, the path or the practice, ask now. Don't regret later that you were face to face with the teacher and didn't ask. Silence. He asks a second time. Silence. A third time. Silence. Maybe you're holding back out of respect for me, he says; then tell a friend, and let the friend ask. Still silence. Ananda says it's wonderful: not one monk here has any doubt. Picture that room. A teacher who could have closed with a speech instead spends his last minutes asking three times, is anything unclear? It's the open hand once more. If the teaching is going to be the teacher, it had better be understood.
screen: `WE HAVE NO TEACHER? DON'T SEE IT THAT WAY.` · `DHAMMA AND VINAYA WILL TEACH YOU.` · `NO SUCCESSOR NAMED.` · `ANY DOUBTS? ASKED THREE TIMES.` · then, large: `THE TEACHING IS THE TEACHER.`

segments.voice: Sit as if a teacher you trust were in the room. Not watching you critically, just present. Let your posture settle the way it would if they were there. Breathe the way they'd remind you to breathe. Then let the picture go, and keep the posture and the breath. Notice that what they taught is still here, in your back and in your lungs. The bell holds the time.
The teaching as teacher. The Buddha's words at Kusinara: when I am gone, the Dhamma and the discipline I taught will be your teacher. Today's word.
Your line: the teaching is the teacher. Today, when you're unsure what to do, ask what a teaching you trust already says, and let it teach you. Day five hundred fifty-one.

howItsDone: Theravada monastics treat the Dhamma and Vinaya as their teacher, reciting the monastic rules every fortnight, and many Buddhist schools also honor living lineages of teachers who pass the teaching on.

fork.setup: you're the Buddha, about to pass away. your students will soon think they have no teacher. what do you tell them?
options: choose the wisest among you to lead.
the teaching and the discipline I gave you will be your teacher.
fork.reveal: the Dhamma and Vinaya will be their teacher. then he asks three times if anyone has a doubt.

original.note: Pali dhammavinaya: the teaching and the discipline, the Buddha's name for what he left behind.

trapdoor: what you thought: when a founder dies, someone takes his place.
what it means: the Buddha says the teaching and the discipline themselves will be the teacher.
what a scholar hears: DN 16's yo vo ananda maya dhammo ca vinayo ca desito pannatto, so vo mamaccayena sattha is a key text for authority in early Buddhism, with no personal successor named.

sources.ref: Digha Nikaya 16 (Mahaparinibbana Sutta), the Dhamma-Vinaya as teacher and the last questions

notes: DN 16 paraphrased. Confirm the Pali in the scholar floor and the three-times invitation to ask, including the suggestion to ask through a friend.
